title: Retail Pharmacy Network Benefit — Emergency Supply Already Authorised and the Vacation Supply
content:
**Rule.** Under the Retail Pharmacy Network Benefit, supply already authorised for the drug is also taken off the vacation supply:

- when an emergency supply for the drug was granted within the last seven days and no claim has used it yet, its full days are taken off;
- when the most recent emergency supply for the drug has already been used by a claim, the days of that claim not yet run out are taken off;
- otherwise nothing is taken off.

**Terms used.** The emergency supply looked at is the most recent emergency-supply override granted for the drug on the benefit. "Within the last seven days" means granted today or on any of the seven calendar days before today. An emergency supply has been "used by a claim" when a paid retail claim was filled under that override; the days of that claim not yet run out are its days supply less the calendar days from its date of service (day zero) to today, never below zero.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical; the emergency supply allowed 5 days)

| Most recent emergency supply for the drug | Used by a paid claim | Taken off the vacation supply |
|---|---|---|
| Granted 7 days before today | No | 5 days |
| Granted 8 days before today | No | Nothing |
| Granted today | No | 5 days |
| Granted 3 days ago; claim of 5 days filled under it 2 days ago | Yes | 5 less 2, that is 3 days |
| Granted 20 days ago; claim of 5 days filled under it 18 days ago | Yes | 0 days (never below zero) |
| No emergency supply for the drug on record | — | Nothing |

The case of a used emergency supply does not depend on how long ago it was granted; only the claim's days not yet run out matter.
